section_title: Review problem and internal scientific thesis
scientific_question: Why does this literature require an evidence-weighted mechanism review rather than parallel topical summaries?
section_objective: State the internal thesis and motivate the wave–spray–mixture–ignition chain.
opening_problem: Local component physics is much better resolved than its end-to-end HPDI coupling.
mechanism_logic: separately supported domains → explicit transfer audit → review thesis
key_parameters: contextual NPR; Mach context; We; loading duration; ΔSOI
required_boundary_conditions: evidence directness and application distance
required_caution: Do not present the complete chain as observed.
key_takeaway: The review contribution is to distinguish strong component closures from four explicit cross-scale discontinuities.
transition_to_next: Define scope, terminology, and evidence hierarchy.
notes: Background/framing section; draft after mechanism chapters.

section_title: Scope, terminology, and evidence-status discipline
scientific_question: What counts as comparable evidence across injection, shock, droplet, spray, and combustion domains?
section_objective: Define evidence classes, application directness, and comparison rules.
opening_problem: Identical symbols often represent different physical states and source roles.
mechanism_logic: source hierarchy → definition matching → direct/mixed/cross-scale/gap labels
key_parameters: NPR; Mach; We; Re; Oh; loading duration; breakup time
required_boundary_conditions: pressure role/type; reference frame; event definition
required_caution: Do not normalize incompatible definitions into apparent comparability.
key_takeaway: Definition compatibility is a scientific boundary, not a formatting detail.
transition_to_next: Introduce the article-level mechanism framework.

section_title: Article framework and narrative route
scientific_question: How will the article progress from injection boundary to combustion while preserving open arrows?
section_objective: Preview the chapter sequence and evidence-status encoding.
opening_problem: A linear narrative can falsely imply every arrow has equal support.
mechanism_logic: injection → wave → loading → droplet → fragments → mixture → ignition; plus bounded RDE analogue
key_parameters: cross-scale parameter bridge
required_boundary_conditions: direct/indirect/cross-scale/gap encoding
required_caution: Preview gaps without resolving them rhetorically.
key_takeaway: The article follows mechanism progression and revisits gaps at their first physical location.
transition_to_next: Begin with the time-dependent injection boundary.

section_title: Definition-complete injection and ambient boundary state
scientific_question: Which injector, nozzle, ambient, gas, and pressure definitions are required before underexpanded-jet comparisons are meaningful?
section_objective: Establish the complete upstream state and comparability filters.
opening_problem: Nominal injection pressure and generic NPR collapse non-equivalent physical boundaries.
mechanism_logic: pressure role/type + nozzle + ambient + gas state → contextual underexpansion boundary
key_parameters: p_inj; ambient p/T/ρ; nozzle D/L/D/shape; gas properties; contextual NPR
required_boundary_conditions: fixed NPR versus fixed injection pressure; geometry and species matching
required_caution: Do not claim monotonic penetration or mixing trends across unmatched geometries.
key_takeaway: The injection boundary is multivariable and must be typed before scaling.
transition_to_next: Add time-resolved valve and pressure development to this boundary.

section_title: Injector pressure build-up and developing underexpanded state
scientific_question: How do pressure build-up and valve opening distinguish developing from quasi-steady jet states?
section_objective: Describe event-aligned jet formation without replacing it with a plateau NPR.
opening_problem: Steady boundary values cannot reconstruct formation, overshoot, or stabilization.
mechanism_logic: p_inj(t) + valve opening → choking/underexpansion onset → evolving jet state → shock motion
key_parameters: p_inj(t); NPR(t); valve state; formation time; shock position history
required_boundary_conditions: pressure location/type and time reference; event alignment
required_caution: A paper-conditioned choking threshold is not a universal value.
key_takeaway: Mach-disk state is an evolving observable tied to injector history.
transition_to_next: Resolve which shock-topology observables are comparison-ready.

section_title: Mach-disk and shock-cell organization under compatible states
scientific_question: Which shock-structure trends are robust when NPR, state, geometry, and gas species are compatible?
section_objective: Separate well-constrained Mach-disk position from less mature topology metrics.
opening_problem: The same NPR label can hide different pressure roles and gas states.
mechanism_logic: compatible underexpanded state → Mach-disk formation/location → shock-cell topology → near/far-field structure
key_parameters: NPR; x_MD/D; Mach-disk diameter; shock-cell spacing; gas species
required_boundary_conditions: state qualifier; D basis; feature definition; near/far field
required_caution: Do not imply universal diameter, cell-spacing, or potential-core correlations.
key_takeaway: Mach-disk position is the most comparison-ready topology observable when definitions match.
transition_to_next: Ask how this topology changes the local gas state around liquid.
notes: Keep review-secondary GC-0015 as evidence-coverage context.

section_title: Shock, vortex, and wave topology as local gas-state sources
scientific_question: How can near-field shocks, spray-generated waves, and reflected shocks change local pressure, velocity, and spray response?
section_objective: Establish the gas-state side of the loading bridge and distinguish wave origins.
opening_problem: Observed topology or cone-angle changes do not directly specify droplet-level forcing.
mechanism_logic: shock/vortex topology → local p/ρ/u variation → spray-scale response under wave-specific histories
key_parameters: p(x,t); ρ(x,t); u(x,t); local Mach; wave origin; spray angle/penetration
required_boundary_conditions: injector-generated versus reflected wave; hot dense ambient; location and stage
required_caution: Do not equate reflected-shock spray response with injector-generated near-nozzle shocks.
key_takeaway: Gas-state variation is supported, but its droplet exposure must be measured locally.
transition_to_next: Audit the missing topology-to-pilot-loading transfer directly.

section_title: The unclosed shock-topology-to-HPDI-pilot-loading bridge
scientific_question: Does underexpanded-jet shock topology map to the local loading history of actual HPDI pilot droplets?
section_objective: Make MP-033 and KG-001 explicit and specify closure evidence.
opening_problem: B-library topology and C-library loading are independently supported but not co-located in HPDI.
mechanism_logic: Mach disk/shock cells → local state candidate → [MP-033 evidence gap] → pilot-droplet loading
key_parameters: local pressure/velocity jumps; M_rel; loading duration; pilot d0 distribution
required_boundary_conditions: synchronized geometry, chronology, frame, and gas/liquid diagnostics
required_caution: Plausible component relations do not validate the application arrow.
key_takeaway: MP-033 is the first major discontinuity in the HPDI mechanism chain.
transition_to_next: Define magnitude and duration variables usable in canonical droplet response.
notes: Primary full discussion location for GC-0052.

section_title: Loading magnitude, duration, and response-time compatibility
scientific_question: Which local variables and typed intervals are required to describe finite compressible loading?
section_objective: Build the gas-state-to-droplet parameter bridge without proposing a universal new group.
opening_problem: Shock-front passage, shocked-state exposure, and total forcing are not interchangeable.
mechanism_logic: Δp + Δu + local gas state + typed duration → nondimensional response state; τ_loading/τ_response remains hypothesis
key_parameters: Δp; Δu; M_s; M_rel; typed loading duration; τ_loading/τ_response candidate
required_boundary_conditions: state pair; frame; interval start/end events; response-time definition
required_caution: Do not present τ_loading/τ_response as literature-established.
key_takeaway: Droplet loading requires both magnitude and a typed forcing history.
transition_to_next: Use that multivariable state to organize deformation and breakup.
notes: Candidate metric stays project hypothesis only.

section_title: Multivariable compressible droplet-response state
scientific_question: Why can Weber number alone not collapse compressible droplet response?
section_objective: Define the comparison-ready response state and condition-specific regime evidence.
opening_problem: Equal reported We can coexist with different Mach frames, sizes, liquids, and loading histories.
mechanism_logic: M_s/M_rel + definition-complete We/Re/Oh + d0 + duration → deformation/breakup tendency
key_parameters: M_s; M_rel; We; Re; Oh; density ratio; d0; loading duration
required_boundary_conditions: component references; physical stage; liquid state; observation window
required_caution: Do not convert reported ranges into universal critical-We boundaries.
key_takeaway: Comparable We does not guarantee comparable response when Mach context and forcing history differ.
transition_to_next: Examine how external loading generates internal wave and deformation structure.

section_title: Internal wave dynamics and deformation topology
scientific_question: How do shock transmission, focusing, circulation, and front curvature imprint later deformation?
section_objective: Separate internal wave mechanisms from external aerodynamic loading.
opening_problem: Bulk We-based descriptions omit early internal pressure extrema and circulation.
mechanism_logic: incident/local loading → transmission/refraction/focusing → pressure/circulation topology → deformation
key_parameters: shock strength; wave-speed ratio; phase state; curvature; local pressure extrema
required_boundary_conditions: 2D/3D geometry; cavitation/phase change omissions; planar/divergent forcing
required_caution: Do not generalize a modeled divergent-shock result beyond its omitted physics.
key_takeaway: Internal wave history can precondition deformation but is state- and geometry-dependent.
transition_to_next: Follow deformation into competing interfacial instabilities.

section_title: Instability competition and multiscale breakup cascade
scientific_question: How do RT, KH/shear, capillary, sheet, wake, and ligament processes select breakup pathways?
section_objective: Explain breakup as a mechanism competition rather than a Weber-only taxonomy.
opening_problem: A single regime label hides staged sheets, rims, ligaments, and recurrent shedding.
mechanism_logic: deformation structures → competing instabilities → sheet/ligament events → secondary breakup
key_parameters: We; Mach context; Oh; loading duration; breakup event and mode
required_boundary_conditions: taxonomy; forcing history; first versus later shedding
required_caution: Do not conceal the C004 source limitation in broad taxonomy statements.
key_takeaway: Secondary breakup reflects condition-dependent instability competition and staged fragmentation.
transition_to_next: Evaluate what present models and labels can actually predict.
notes: C004 limitation appears at first broad-taxonomy use.

section_title: Regime and model predictive limits
scientific_question: Which response outputs can reduced breakup models and regime maps predict reliably?
section_objective: Bound model-based claims and separate morphology labels from product-state prediction.
opening_problem: Validation against one observable does not establish prediction of fragments, clouds, evaporation, or phase coupling.
mechanism_logic: model assumptions + condition domain → selected response observables; no universal multistage closure
key_parameters: model type; breakup event; fragment metrics; cloud length; evaporation time
required_boundary_conditions: validation observable; condition range; source-specific TAB statement
required_caution: A paper-conditioned TAB success does not establish full-condition predictive coverage.
key_takeaway: A breakup label or one matched deformation history is insufficient for downstream transport and phase-change prediction.
transition_to_next: Introduce interaction mechanisms missing from isolated-droplet models.
notes: GC-0051 is context, not a general endorsement.

section_title: Ordered-droplet shielding, squeeze flow, and channel closure
scientific_question: How do tandem and parallel arrangements change effective loading and breakup?
section_objective: Identify direct multidroplet mechanisms and their arrangement-specific directions.
opening_problem: A universal critical spacing is incompatible with distinct tandem and parallel flow mechanisms.
mechanism_logic: arrangement + S/D → shielding or channel/squeeze flow → redistributed loading → changed deformation/breakup
key_parameters: S/D; arrangement; We; droplet size; relative position
required_boundary_conditions: tandem versus parallel; spacing basis; shock/loading state
required_caution: Do not average opposite arrangement effects into one spacing law.
key_takeaway: Neighbor effects are mechanistic and geometry-specific.
transition_to_next: Scale from ordered droplets to cloud-level feedback on the wave.

section_title: Cloud-scale shock attenuation and feedback
scientific_question: How do droplet populations attenuate and reshape transmitted shock histories?
section_objective: Show the feedback from population state to gas loading.
opening_problem: Ignoring fragmentation can overpredict transmitted pressure through a cloud.
mechanism_logic: exchange area + volume fraction + d0 + breakup → attenuation/reshaping → altered downstream loading
key_parameters: volume fraction; exchange area; d0; shock strength; transmitted pressure/impulse
required_boundary_conditions: dilute cloud; breakup closure; pressure metric
required_caution: Dilute-cloud attenuation is not a validated dense reacting-spray law.
key_takeaway: The dispersed phase changes its own subsequent loading environment.
transition_to_next: Audit transfer from ordered/dilute systems to dense HPDI sprays.

section_title: Canonical-to-dense-spray transfer audit
scientific_question: Which canonical mechanisms survive, and what collective descriptors are missing for dense HPDI pilot sprays?
section_objective: Deploy MP-032 and KG-002 as a central scale-transfer boundary.
opening_problem: Dense sprays add polydispersity, disorder, turbulence, phase change, collisions, and reaction.
mechanism_logic: isolated/ordered mechanisms + collective corrections → [MP-032 not validated] → dense HPDI spray response
key_parameters: size distribution; spacing distribution; volume fraction; turbulence; thermal/reaction state
required_boundary_conditions: population realism and synchronized local loading
required_caution: Do not apply single-droplet regimes directly to pilot spray.
key_takeaway: MP-032 prevents quantitative transfer without population and thermochemical correction.
transition_to_next: Track the fragment population that any successful transfer must predict.

section_title: Fragment population state and transport
scientific_question: Which breakup products, rather than regime labels, control downstream cloud transport?
section_objective: Define fragment size, velocity, spacing, mass, and time as the post-breakup state.
opening_problem: Mean size or breakup mode alone cannot initialize transport and evaporation.
mechanism_logic: secondary breakup → evolving fragment PDF/velocity/spacing → cloud transport and dispersion
key_parameters: fragment PDF; D10/D32; velocity; spacing; mass weighting; sampling time
required_boundary_conditions: detection threshold; statistic weighting; wave history; population density
required_caution: Do not substitute a single mean fragment size for an evolving distribution.
key_takeaway: Fragment population state is the necessary mediator between breakup and downstream transport.
transition_to_next: Examine when fragmenting droplets also undergo significant phase change.

section_title: Overlap of breakup, evaporation, and droplet survival scales
scientific_question: When do breakup and evaporation occur on comparable time scales?
section_objective: Define size- and history-conditioned overlap without asserting a universal threshold.
opening_problem: Evaporation-only models may misrepresent survival when fragmentation changes area and scale.
mechanism_logic: d0/fragment size + wave/thermal history → overlapping breakup and evaporation → altered survival/cloud evolution
key_parameters: d0; fragment size; gas T; volatility; M_rel; evaporation time/length
required_boundary_conditions: size; liquid; observation interval; bow-shock pressure rise; post-wave state
required_caution: A >100 μm early-deformation result does not extend to smaller or later-stage droplets.
key_takeaway: Breakup–evaporation overlap is scale- and history-dependent.
transition_to_next: Resolve why phase change can suppress or promote deformation.

section_title: Conditional direction of phase-change coupling
scientific_question: Why can vaporization suppress deformation in some cases and thermal property changes promote breakup in others?
section_objective: Reconcile apparently opposing findings through boundary conditions.
opening_problem: Opposite directions arise from different thermal and interfacial mechanisms, not necessarily contradiction.
mechanism_logic: vapor layer/Stefan flow → reduced shear versus heating → lower surface tension → conditional response direction
key_parameters: Stefan number; density ratio; volatility; gas T; surface tension; We
required_boundary_conditions: liquid; thermal state; model coefficients; d0; observation interval
required_caution: Do not state a universal sign for breakup–phase-change coupling.
key_takeaway: The coupling direction changes with the dominant interfacial and thermal mechanism.
transition_to_next: Ask whether these fragment/evaporation changes are measured in HPDI mixture fields.

section_title: The unclosed shock-fragment-to-mixture bridge
scientific_question: Does shock-mediated breakup and evaporation measurably alter the HPDI mixture field?
section_objective: Deploy MP-028 and the upstream half of GC-0053 without causal overclosure.
opening_problem: General transport/evaporation physics is not direct evidence of a shock-generated HPDI mixture change.
mechanism_logic: fragment state → transport/evaporation → general mixture contribution; [MP-028 gap] shock-specific measured HPDI redistribution
key_parameters: fragment distribution; evaporation scale; mixture fraction/species field; chronology
required_boundary_conditions: hot dense chamber; walls; turbulence; volatility; synchronized diagnostics
required_caution: Do not claim shock-enhanced mixture preparation from stitched component evidence.
key_takeaway: MP-028 remains the downstream transport-to-application discontinuity.
transition_to_next: Contrast the open shock contribution with direct HPDI chronology and mixture evidence.
notes: Primary full discussion location for GC-0053.

section_title: Injection chronology, geometry, and mixture preparation
scientific_question: How do signed pilot/main timing, overlap geometry, and injector arrangement shape HPDI premixing and stratification?
section_objective: Establish the direct application chain from injection controls to mixture state.
opening_problem: Timing magnitude without fuel order and event definitions is ambiguous.
mechanism_logic: signed chronology + geometry → overlap/entrainment/wall interaction → premixing and stratification
key_parameters: ΔSOI; dwell; overlap; injection duration; hole arrangement; mixture metrics
required_boundary_conditions: fuel order; sign convention; geometry; operating point; review-secondary status
required_caution: Do not treat a review-secondary control statement as primary confirmation.
key_takeaway: Chronology and geometry directly reorganize mixture preparation, with condition-specific outcomes.
transition_to_next: Connect mixture and pilot-product distribution to ignition.

section_title: Pilot-product interaction and ignition response
scientific_question: When does pilot/main overlap assist main-fuel ignition, and when can it disrupt or delay the pilot?
section_objective: Synthesize direct and qualified evidence for mixture-to-ignition coupling.
opening_problem: Overlap has stage- and geometry-dependent directions.
mechanism_logic: mixture/pilot-product distribution → chemical/thermal interaction → ignition timing/location
key_parameters: ΔSOI; ignition delay; EOI; temperature; O/H/OH radical state; overlap geometry
required_boundary_conditions: ignition definition; fuel pair; ambient reactivity; transport versus 0D kinetics
required_caution: Keep dilution and radical explanations at their reported evidence level.
key_takeaway: Mixture and pilot-product state directly govern ignition, but the direction depends on chronology and geometry.
transition_to_next: Follow ignition chronology into heat release and operating response.

section_title: Heat-release mode, injection pressure, and operating response
scientific_question: How do injection pressure, pilot energy, and timing shape heat-release mode and performance tradeoffs?
section_objective: Bound direct combustion-response evidence by operating condition.
opening_problem: Improved mixing can coexist with emissions, pressure-rise, or stability penalties.
mechanism_logic: injection/ignition chronology → heat-release mode → condition-dependent combustion response
key_parameters: injection pressure; energy share; CA50; AHRR; load; timing
required_boundary_conditions: pressure definition; load/speed; energy share; diagnostic definition
required_caution: Do not generalize paper-specific feasibility or regime labels beyond tested conditions.
key_takeaway: Combustion benefits and penalties remain operating-point dependent even when mixing is intensified.
transition_to_next: Localize additional H2 heat-release claims without broad generalization.

section_title: Condition-specific hydrogen heat-release behavior
scientific_question: What condition-specific H2 heat-release patterns are reported, and how should they be used?
section_objective: Deploy remaining paper-conditioned combustion claims as bounded application evidence.
opening_problem: Single-source AHRR and comparative-fuel statements do not define universal HPDI behavior.
mechanism_logic: fuel-specific injection/combustion duration and properties → reported AHRR pattern → bounded interpretation
key_parameters: injection duration; combustion duration; AHRR/HRR; fuel properties
required_boundary_conditions: paper source condition; diagnostic and fuel comparison
required_caution: Do not merge localized AHRR claims into a cross-paper universal rule.
key_takeaway: Paper-conditioned heat-release observations support context, not universal scaling.
transition_to_next: Return to the untested upstream shock-mediated cause.

section_title: The unclosed shock-caused mixture-to-ignition link
scientific_question: Does a shock-caused mixture change produce a measurable HPDI ignition or combustion response?
section_objective: Deploy MP-029 and distinguish it from the directly supported timing chain.
opening_problem: Direct timing-to-ignition evidence does not identify an upstream shock cause.
mechanism_logic: direct: chronology → mixture → ignition; open: shock → fragments/evaporation → mixture → [MP-029 gap] ignition
key_parameters: shock chronology; species field; ignition delay/location; heat release
required_boundary_conditions: synchronized shock, mixture, ignition, and heat-release measurement
required_caution: Never write that shock improves HPDI ignition as an established result.
key_takeaway: MP-029 is not closed by the strong direct evidence for timing-controlled ignition.
transition_to_next: Use RDE/detonation only as a bounded strong-wave analogue.

section_title: Droplet and evaporation scales in detonation and RDE wave response
scientific_question: How do droplet size and typed evaporation scales affect wave structure, multiplicity, speed, and stability?
section_objective: Synthesize characteristic-scale coupling within the strong-wave domain.
opening_problem: Scale ratios are meaningful only within their stated reaction, refill, and geometry definitions.
mechanism_logic: d0 and evaporation scale relative to reaction/refill/wave scale → vaporization completeness → wave response
key_parameters: d0; evaporation length/time; L_E/L_D; wave number; wave-relative position
required_boundary_conditions: fuel; chemistry; pre-vaporized fraction; geometry; scale definitions
required_caution: Keep L_E/L_D within its defined RDE system.
key_takeaway: Characteristic-scale coupling is supported within RDE/detonation conditions.
transition_to_next: Compare reacting and inert post-wave droplet histories.

section_title: Reacting versus inert strong-wave droplet loading
scientific_question: Why can equal leading-shock Mach produce different later droplet response in detonation and inert shocks?
section_objective: Separate early leading-wave similarity from later reacting-history divergence.
opening_problem: Leading-shock Mach does not determine post-wave velocity, sound speed, chemistry, gradients, or duration.
mechanism_logic: matched leading Mach → similar early topology; reacting post-wave history → divergent cavitation/deformation/breakup
key_parameters: detonation/incident Mach; post-wave velocity; d0; breakup time; loading duration
required_boundary_conditions: liquid; wave strength; chemistry; post-wave state and event definition
required_caution: Do not transfer inert-shock correlations using leading Mach alone.
key_takeaway: Reacting post-wave history, not leading Mach alone, governs later response divergence.
transition_to_next: Audit what, if anything, transfers from strong-wave applications to HPDI.

section_title: Bounded transfer from strong-wave analogues to HPDI
scientific_question: Which RDE/detonation insights are qualitatively transferable to HPDI and which are not validated?
section_objective: Deploy MP-034 and KG-008 as an application boundary.
opening_problem: Shared strong-wave terminology does not establish application-scale equivalence.
mechanism_logic: strong-wave mechanism insight + typed scale comparison → bounded analogue; [MP-034] no direct HPDI validation
key_parameters: Mach context; We; L_E/L_D; chemistry; residence and injection scales
required_boundary_conditions: validated nondimensional mapping; reaction and geometry matching
required_caution: RDE evidence cannot prove HPDI strong-wave behavior.
key_takeaway: RDE/detonation is a bounded analogue, not substitute HPDI evidence.
transition_to_next: Integrate all component closures and open paths into one evidence map.

section_title: Closed components and unclosed cross-scale pathways
scientific_question: Which mechanism links are directly supported, indirect, cross-scale, or missing?
section_objective: Reassemble all MP pathways with evidence-status and application-distance encoding.
opening_problem: A continuous arrow chain can visually overstate closure.
mechanism_logic: closed domain-bounded links + explicit MP-033/032/028/029 discontinuities → evidence-weighted framework
key_parameters: whole parameter bridge
required_boundary_conditions: evidence directness; cross-scale status; condition compatibility
required_caution: Do not smooth over discontinuities in the final synthesis.
key_takeaway: The article's novelty is an explicit map of what is closed, what transfers only qualitatively, and what remains unmeasured.
transition_to_next: Convert each gap into a specific evidence requirement.

section_title: Evidence-derived research priorities and diagnostic requirements
scientific_question: What measurements, simulations, and definition standards would most efficiently close the priority gaps?
section_objective: Deploy KG-001–KG-010 as staged research needs.
opening_problem: Generic calls for more data do not identify which arrow or definition needs closure.
mechanism_logic: gap location → required co-located variables → condition matching → validation target
key_parameters: p(x,t); u(x,t); droplet/fragment PDFs; species fields; ignition/heat release; definition-complete ratios
required_boundary_conditions: synchronized chronology; geometry; dense reacting state; uncertainty
required_caution: Keep C004 as a source-availability limitation, not a scientific mechanism gap.
key_takeaway: Priority experiments must close specific arrows with synchronized, definition-complete measurements.
transition_to_next: Conclude with bounded contributions and no new mechanism claims.

section_title: Conclusions and review contributions
scientific_question: What can the review conclude without overstating cross-scale closure?
section_objective: Restate the internal thesis, contributions, and bounded research priorities.
opening_problem: Conclusions can accidentally upgrade synthesis propositions into universal facts.
mechanism_logic: chapter findings → bounded contributions → explicit unclosed paths → Phase 13 conclusion
key_parameters: definition discipline and priority diagnostics
required_boundary_conditions: proposition evidence status and application directness
required_caution: No proposition is established or universal.
key_takeaway: The review unifies strong local physics while preserving the incomplete validation of the full HPDI chain.
transition_to_next: NA
